title: Reshaping, Transposing & More 🔄
description: Master reshape, transpose, expand_dims, and squeeze to juggle dimensions.

slides.title: Reshape Revisited ✨
slides.content:
# `tf.reshape(tensor, shape)`

- Changes the view, **not** the data.
- Total elements must match.
- Use `-1` to infer a dimension.

```python
t = tf.constant([1,2,3,4,5,6])
tf.reshape(t, [2,3])      # 2×3
tf.reshape(t, [2,-1])     # -1 → inferred as 3
```

> Analogy: Rearranging the same set of books into different stacks.

quizData.question: What will `tf.reshape([1,2,3,4], [2, -1])` return?
quizData.explanation: With 4 elements, `-1` infers 2 columns, giving shape (2,2).

slides.title: Transpose: Swap Axes 🔁
slides.codeSnippet:
import tensorflow as tf

t = tf.constant([[1,2,3],[4,5,6]])  # (2,3)
print(tf.transpose(t).shape)        # (3,2)

# 3D example
t3 = tf.constant([[[1],[2]],[[3],[4]],[[5],[6]]])  # (3,2,1)
# move last axis to first: perm=[2,1,0]
transposed = tf.transpose(t3, perm=[2,1,0])
print(transposed.shape)  # (1,2,3)

quizData.question: If `a` has shape `(2,3,4)`, what is the shape of `tf.transpose(a, perm=[2,0,1])`?
quizData.explanation: Permutation [2,0,1] puts axis 2 first, then 0, then 1. So shape becomes (4,2,3).

slides.title: Adding & Removing Dimensions 🧬
slides.content:
# `tf.expand_dims` & `tf.squeeze`

- `expand_dims(tensor, axis)`: inserts a new dimension of size 1 at the given axis.
- `squeeze(tensor, axis)`: removes dimensions of size 1.

Use case: adapting a single image (28,28) to batch of 1: (1,28,28).

slides.title: Expand & Squeeze in Action
slides.codeSnippet:
img = tf.ones((28,28))
batch = tf.expand_dims(img, axis=0)  # shape (1,28,28)
print(batch.shape)

flat = tf.squeeze(batch, axis=0)     # back to (28,28)
print(flat.shape)

slides.title: Flatten with Reshape 📏
slides.content: Often you need a 1D version. Use `tf.reshape(t, [-1])`. For a full flatten preserving batch, do `tf.reshape(t, [batch_size, -1])`.
